name: montera34/airbnb.barcelona
what_it_holds: Repo from a 2018 participatory data workshop on Airbnb/touristification in Barcelona. Contains Inside-Airbnb-sourced snapshots under data/original/airbnb/ at multiple dated pulls between 150430 (30 Apr 2015) and 190308 (8 Mar 2019), each with listings_summary_barcelona_insideairbnb.csv and reviews_summary_barcelona_insideairbnb.csv (large listings.csv.gz not stored in repo), plus geographic boundary shapefiles and Barcelona demographic/housing (population, dwelling) tables for overlay analysis.
why_useful: Barcelona Inside Airbnb history back to April 2015 -- earlier than our current 13-city panel (Dec 2022 onward) and directly relevant to the Garcia-Lopez et al. Barcelona housing-impact replication literature named in this theme; also usable to sanity-check current Barcelona ADR/listing trends against a much longer base period.

name: airbnb-occupancy-tax
what_it_holds: Economics honors thesis studying Boston's Airbnb occupancy-tax implementation (2018-2019). Committed Jupyter notebooks (e.g. 'Calculate Exits.ipynb') and CSVs with listing-level reservation-date metrics (weekly/bimonthly/monthly aggregations), 'date booked' monthly aggregation, and an entries/exits analysis. Treatment city Boston plus control cities Montreal, Providence/Rhode Island, Washington DC, Quebec City, Nashville, San Francisco, Chicago, Twin Cities, Denver, Asheville, with a control-city tax-rate spreadsheet. Filters to listings booked >14 nights/year (the tax threshold) and applies synthetic-control methodology around each city's tax-implementation date.
why_useful: Direct academic precedent for imputing occupancy/nights from Airbnb review cadence around a lodging-tax event (methodologically close to the team's own reviews-based stays index, gap #2/#3 realised-occupancy proxies and tax pass-through). Small city-year panel, not itself a broad tax-collections dataset, but a usable cross-check dataset and method.
themes: State and city hotel occupancy and lodging-tax datasets (Nevada, Florida tourist development tax, Texas hotel occupancy tax, California TOT, NYC hotel occupancy tax, Hawaii TAT)
Tourist tax and city-tax datasets: Paris taxe de sejour, Amsterdam toeristenbelasting, Italian imposta di soggiorno, Airbnb remittance reports, occupancy-tax remittance by platform
why_all: Direct academic precedent for imputing occupancy/nights from Airbnb review cadence around a lodging-tax event (methodologically close to the team's own reviews-based stays index, gap #2/#3 realised-occupancy proxies and tax pass-through). Small city-year panel, not itself a broad tax-collections dataset, but a usable cross-check dataset and method.

Directly on-theme: a natural-experiment dataset on how STR occupancy-tax implementation affects Airbnb listing/booking behavior across 11 North American cities, with before/after listing-level data. Could inform how new occupancy-tax regimes (gap #12 regulation trackers, also relevant to nights/ADR elasticity work) affect nights and host supply; a template for a similar study on newer tax rollouts.

name: Open Source Asset Pricing (Chen-Zimmermann) CrossSection
what_it_holds: Code (WRDS pull in Python, portfolio construction in R) reproducing 300+ published cross-sectional return anomalies, including an 'EarningsSurprise.csv' signal and (per the project's data portal) an Earnings Announcement Return / SUE-style anomaly among the documented signals. Pre-built signal and portfolio-return files are distributed off-repo at openassetpricing.com rather than committed in git.
why_useful: The EarningsSurprise / SUE-family signal underlying the classic earnings-drift anomaly is exactly the academic analogue of an 'earnings-drift dataset' — could be used to benchmark whether an ABNB-style earnings-drift effect is even a real base rate in the broader market before building any drift trade thesis.
size_hint: 300+ signals, decades of US cross-section, WRDS-derived
themes: Options and event-move tooling: historical option chains (CBOE samples, ORATS-like), earnings implied-move calculators, IV term-structure datasets, earnings-drift datasets
why_all: The EarningsSurprise / SUE-family signal underlying the classic earnings-drift anomaly is exactly the academic analogue of an 'earnings-drift dataset' — could be used to benchmark whether an ABNB-style earnings-drift effect is even a real base rate in the broader market before building any drift trade thesis.

name: Post-Earnings-Announcement-Drift (investor attention)
what_it_holds: Jupyter-notebook replication package (11 commits) of the PEAD anomaly using a standard event-study/CAR framework over an event window t=0 to t=21. Adds Google Trends search volume as an investor-attention proxy (following Da, Engelberg & Gao 2011) and an 'earnings announcement congestion' measure (competing same-day earnings releases) to test delayed information incorporation. Reports an annualized Sharpe of ~1.76 for a resulting long-short strategy. Contains cached datasets, figures, and tables in output folders (exact tickers/row counts not stated in README).
why_useful: A ready-made PEAD + investor-attention replication combining exactly the two themes in scope (event-study drift, and a Google-Trends-as-attention-proxy method) -- useful as a template even though our team's own Google Trends test failed as a demand nowcast; this is a different application (attention/congestion, not level).
time_coverage: unspecified (uses Google Trends, so likely post-2011)
duplicate_of_holding: Google Trends already tested and found not to work as a demand nowcast; this is a distinct use (investor attention around earnings dates), not a re-flag of the same failed construction.
themes: Event-study and factor packages; earnings-surprise datasets; post-earnings-drift replication; Ken French factor loaders
why_all: A ready-made PEAD + investor-attention replication combining exactly the two themes in scope (event-study drift, and a Google-Trends-as-attention-proxy method) -- useful as a template even though our team's own Google Trends test failed as a demand nowcast; this is a different application (attention/congestion, not level).

why_useful: Extends regional-mix regulatory coverage (gap #12) into a fast-growing EMEA/emerging market not in our 32-factor database or municipal registry panel; useful context for EMEA nights/ADR mix even if the underlying data turns out thin.
